stages.rough: Edit of the concept. Keep the small rocky mound shored with rough timber frames, the very small dark cave mouth, the spined tail tip coming out of the dark, the rough wooden barrier and the torch on its stake. Remove both guards entirely. Add one great grey bone lying in front of the mouth, and two big round lifting stones worn smooth on top beside the barrier. A real, modest, slightly worrying place, no joke. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. No letters, no runes, no loose cloth, no hard-edged ground slab, a feathered patch of natural ground on the same footprint, no painted cast shadows, no grey smoke or fog. The grey diamond is only a size guide and is not part of the picture: no grey anywhere, the grass and earth of the ground end in a ragged natural edge straight onto the magenta. Matte paint, no gloss.
stages.solid: The same lair one step on, painted between rough and grand. The mound rises into a real outcrop of bare rock. The timber props give way to a door frame of squared, roughly dressed stone with iron straps, the barrier becomes a heavy iron-bound gate standing half open. The tail is thicker, and a spined back shows in the dark. Three big half-buried ribs in the ground, the lifting stones now a graded row of three, two torches, a stiff wooden pennant on a pole. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. No letters, no runes, no loose cloth, no hard-edged ground slab, a feathered patch of natural ground on the same footprint, no painted cast shadows, no grey smoke or fog. stages.grand: Edit of the concept. Keep the cliff with its mossy overhang, the two great tapered stone pillars with iron bands, the beam across them, the wooden gate, the path and both half-buried dragon skeletons. Remove both guards. Remove all the fog. Remove the small red tabs on the beam. Inside the cave, deep in the shadow, exactly one dragon head with closed eyes lying at rest, and nothing else in the dark but bare rock; the banner is a plain solid ochre cloth with no emblem. One long curved rib lashed between two oak posts as a pull-up bar, its middle worn pale, the graded lifting stones beside it, and a clan banner stretched on a rigid wooden frame on one pillar. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. stages.mythic: Edit of the concept, going much further. Remove the fog. Keep the monumental carved portal with its dragon reliefs, the great dragon resting asleep with closed eyes on its heap, and a great heap of old coins spilling out over the threshold in a wide fan that runs down the path and across the open ground in front of the portal, hundreds of coins outside the cave: painted matte, dull ochre and brass discs in big simple masses, no glint, no sparkle. The mountain behind becomes one vertiginous needle of rock rising almost to the top of the canvas, complete, not cropped on any side, around which one immense stone dragon is carved in deep relief, body coiling up the peak, its closed-eyed head forming the summit. New magic: fissures of molten ember orange run through the carved coils and the reliefs from the cave up to the summit, as if the sleeper's breath moves through the mountain, strong enough to read by day. A plain carved shield with ember light in its surface, no symbol, above the portal. The rib bar, the lifting stones and the half-buried bones stay at the foot. No blood, no skull grin. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. No letters, no runes, no loose cloth, no hard-edged ground slab, a feathered patch of natural ground on the same footprint, no painted cast shadows, no grey smoke or fog.
